title: A peaceful, well-maintained campus built around the working day
lead: A perfect blend of academics, sport and cultural activity — with the infrastructure, laboratories and green surroundings that make a dynamic learning atmosphere possible.
intro: The campus sits at 48 Kukde Layout in Rameshwari, opposite the Railway Police Headquarters — a location that is central enough to reach easily and quiet enough to work in.

Everything here is arranged around the school day rather than around a brochure photograph. The laboratories are next to the classrooms that use them. The canteen is where children can actually reach it in a short break. The hall, the basement and the playground carry assembly, rehearsal, examinations and sport in turn.

items.title: Playground, hall & basement
items.summary: The open ground and covered hall that carry assembly, sport, rehearsal and examinations.
description: The playground is the centre of the school day — morning assembly, physical education periods, athletics practice and the annual sports meet all happen here.

The covered hall and basement extend that space through the monsoon and the examination season: they take rehearsals for the annual cultural programme, inter-house competition, indoor games and large written examinations without disrupting timetabled classes.

items.title: Physics laboratory
items.summary: Where science stops being a set of definitions and becomes something a student has actually done.
description: The physics laboratory is timetabled, not occasional. Students set up apparatus, take readings, record observations and account for their own error — which is a different skill from reproducing a result.

Experiments are supervised throughout, and practical journals are checked as carefully as written work. It is the single facility that most changes how our students answer science questions in a board examination.

items.title: Computer laboratory
items.summary: The working home of the junior college practical syllabus, and of computer literacy across the school.
description: Junior college students carry out their practical papers here under supervision, with journals maintained through the year rather than assembled in the final week.
The same laboratory supports computer literacy from the primary grades upward, and hosts the applied sessions of our BCCA degree programme.

items.title: Robotics workshops
items.summary: Hands-on sessions where high school students build, wire and program something that then has to work.
description: Robotics workshops run for high school classes through the session, covering sensing, control and simple autonomous behaviour.
They are deliberately practical: a design that looks right on paper and fails on the floor teaches more in one afternoon than a chapter does in a week.

items.title: Library
items.summary: A quiet room at the centre of the school, and the habit it is there to build.
description: The library supports reading for pleasure alongside reference and project work, with a collection covering fiction, general knowledge, the sciences and the languages taught in school.

Reading periods are timetabled for the younger grades so that borrowing becomes a habit rather than an instruction, and senior students use the space for supervised private study and project research.

items.title: Healthy canteen
items.summary: A canteen facility for students to have a complete, healthy diet — and a proper break in which to eat it.
description: The canteen is there so that children eat well during the school day: a complete and healthy diet, prepared and served on the premises.
It is also, deliberately, a good time for students to refresh themselves and enjoy the environment — the part of the day where friendships across classes actually get made.

items.title: Smart classrooms
items.summary: Technology-enabled teaching spaces used every day, not reserved for demonstrations.
description: Digital teaching boards allow a diagram to be drawn, animated, annotated and revisited — and allow a teacher to return to exactly the frame a student did not follow.
The classrooms themselves are kept simple and well-lit, arranged so that a teacher can reach every desk within a few steps.

items.title: Sports facilities
items.summary: Eight disciplines, from the athletics track to the carrom board.
description: Basketball court, volleyball court, cricket court and nets, an athletics track, table tennis, karate, carrom and a gymnasium — enough breadth that most children find something they are good at.
Physical education is timetabled for every grade, and inter-house competition runs through the year, culminating in the annual Apostolic Sports meet on the school ground.

items.title: Arts, music & theatre
items.summary: Where the annual production is rehearsed, and where a quiet child often finds their voice.
description: Art and craft run from Pre-Primary upward, and the school's annual cultural programme stages full productions rehearsed by students across all four sections.
Music, patriotic singing and elocution are entered for inter-school competition, and our singers have returned with medals and participation certificates.

items.title: Safety & security
items.summary: Full CCTV coverage, guards at the gate and inside, photo ID for every student.
description: The school is under CCTV surveillance, with several guards stationed at the gate and within the premises.

Each student carries an identity card recording their parents' details, and only an authorised person is permitted to interact with or collect a child. Two attendants are assigned to the Pre-Primary section, with two attendants for each of the higher sections.
